Test what a built Android App Bundle or iOS application contains, without a device.

`android_bundle_test` inspects the APK bundletool generates from a godot_app's App Bundle;
`ios_app_test` inspects a godot_app's iOS application. Both run as ordinary Bazel tests on
the execution platform, so a mobile build can be checked where it is built, such as for
the native libraries of an add-on or the resources of the pack. Neither installs nor runs
the application. See [platform prerequisites](../../platforms.md) for the Android SDK and
Xcode setup the applications need.

<a id="android_bundle_test"></a>

## android_bundle_test

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot/testing:artifact_tests.bzl", "android_bundle_test")

android_bundle_test(<a href="#android_bundle_test-name">name</a>, <a href="#android_bundle_test-apk_libraries">apk_libraries</a>, <a href="#android_bundle_test-application_id">application_id</a>, <a href="#android_bundle_test-bundle">bundle</a>, <a href="#android_bundle_test-bundletool">bundletool</a>, <a href="#android_bundle_test-classes">classes</a>, <a href="#android_bundle_test-debug_info">debug_info</a>,
                    <a href="#android_bundle_test-debug_symbols">debug_symbols</a>, <a href="#android_bundle_test-manifest_entries">manifest_entries</a>, <a href="#android_bundle_test-pck_files">pck_files</a>, <a href="#android_bundle_test-symbol_libraries">symbol_libraries</a>)
</pre>

Test an Android App Bundle the way Google Play delivers it, without a device.

The test validates the bundle with bundletool, generates its universal APK and
checks that the APK stores `assets/main.pck` uncompressed and carries the export's
command line, that the base manifest declares `application_id` and Godot's
activity, and every listed manifest entry, native library, Java class and PCK
resource. With `debug_symbols`, each library of the application's symbol ZIP must
match the stripped library the APK packages by GNU build ID and keep its symbol
table. The test fails with the list of what is missing. It writes the evidence,
such as the PCK's resource paths, to `bundle.json` among the test's undeclared
outputs.

The inspection runs on the execution platform with the host JDK, so a bundle built
for an Android platform is inspected on the machine running the test. Build the
bundle with `--@autoload_rules_godot//godot:android_format=aab`; see
[App Bundles](../../platforms.md#app-bundles-for-store-upload).

Example:
```starlark
android_bundle_test(
    name = "app_packages_extension_test",
    bundle = ":app",
    bundletool = "@bundletool//file",
    application_id = "org.example.game",
    apk_libraries = ["lib/arm64-v8a/libgame_native.so"],
    pck_files = ["main/main.gd"],
)
```

`@bundletool//file` is an `http_file` of the checksum-pinned `bundletool-all` JAR
in the caller's `MODULE.bazel`.

### Default outputs
| kind | cardinality | availability | behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| test | one | always | inspect the bundle under bazel test on the execution platform; bundle.json is an undeclared test output |

none

<a id="ios_app_test"></a>

## ios_app_test

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot/testing:artifact_tests.bzl", "ios_app_test")

ios_app_test(<a href="#ios_app_test-name">name</a>, <a href="#ios_app_test-app">app</a>, <a href="#ios_app_test-debug_symbols">debug_symbols</a>, <a href="#ios_app_test-files">files</a>, <a href="#ios_app_test-infoplist_keys">infoplist_keys</a>, <a href="#ios_app_test-symbols">symbols</a>)
</pre>

Test what an iOS application contains, without a simulator or device.

The test reads the application's `.app` directory or unpacks its `.ipa` and checks
that its executable defines every listed C symbol, local ones included, that every
listed file exists in the bundle and that its `Info.plist` has every listed key.
With `debug_symbols`, the application's dSYM must exist and carry the executable's
UUID for each CPU. The test fails with the list of what the application lacks; at
least one check must be requested.

A statically linked extension shows as its entry symbol, such as the
`entry_symbol` of godot_cc_extension. The inspection uses Apple's `nm`, so it runs
on a macOS execution platform with Xcode; see [iOS](../../platforms.md#ios).

Example:
```starlark
ios_app_test(
    name = "app_links_extension_test",
    app = ":app",
    symbols = ["game_native_init"],
    infoplist_keys = ["CFBundleShortVersionString"],
)
```

### Default outputs
| kind | cardinality | availability | behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| test | one | always | inspect the application under bazel test on a macOS execution platform |

### Output groups
none

### Generated targets
none

### Providers
none
